title: Fail loudly when systemd-resolved will not start after networkd retirement
head: 531491999f47
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The new active-service shortcut can strand a disabled resolver on the next boot
leads.consequence: When /etc/resolv.conf uses the resolver stub and systemd-resolved is running but disabled or masked for the next boot, the historical migration returns success without attempting to enable it; the recovery migration likewise exits. omarchy-migrate writes each per-user success marker, but after the next boot the service need not start and stub-backed DNS fails. At 02d1e01e the historical migration's enable --now would have enabled even an already-running service. Keep the no-sudo early return only after checking that the stub's resolver will start on the next boot, or warn/fail rather than mark this state repaired.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus_minor; Same as Opus N12 (active but disabled). Base and recovery migration also leave it disabled; upgrade already ran systemctl enable. Not material.

leads.summary: The stub detection excludes documented systemd-resolved configurations, silently completing with broken DNS
leads.consequence: An inactive resolved with /etc/resolv.conf symlinked to /usr/lib/systemd/resolv.conf (a static file with nameserver 127.0.0.53), or a regular /etc/resolv.conf containing nameserver 127.0.0.53, still needs the local resolver. Both migrations skip these configurations because the link text is neither of two accepted targets or because the file is not a link. On the live upgrade path with NetworkManager already active, the historical migration still retires networkd and returns zero, then the recovery migration also returns zero; the runner stamps both done, so no later login automatically retries DNS repair. The new historical guard changed the former enable attempt into a false success for these modes. Detect actual use of the stub including the static file and plain 127.0.0.53 entries; leave genuine nonstub overrides alone.
leads.triage: dropped; Opus N9/N9b covers static /usr/lib/systemd/resolv.conf. Omarchy writes only the two stub spellings (grep); prior public suggestion asked for stub predicate; lead's live-upgrade premise wrong since upgrade writes stub link at line 1374 before migrations.

leads.summary: An active systemd-resolved does not guarantee that its DNS stub is listening
leads.consequence: With a stub-backed resolv.conf, a resolver that remains active while DNSStubListener=no is configured, CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE is missing, or port 53 was taken can lack the 127.0.0.53 listener. Upstream explicitly warns and disables its stub for an address-in-use or permission failure while continuing to report the manager as started. Both migrations return success based on is-active without checking listener availability; markers are written and retries suppressed although DNS through the configured stub may still fail. Check the stub endpoint if the aim is to fail loudly for this case, or narrow the claimed guarantee to unit activation only. This gap also predates the latest 53149199 commit.
leads.triage: dropped; Stub listener bind failure while unit active predates PR, not specific to 53149199; speculative.

leads.summary: Replacing resolved's restart leaves Quattro's newly written Docker DNS listener unapplied when resolved is already active
leads.consequence: On an upgrade where the historical migration is pending and NetworkManager is already active, the upgrade writes DNSStubListenerExtra=172.17.0.1 and configures Docker to query 172.17.0.1, then enables resolved without starting/reloading an already-active unit. The historical migration now returns at is-active (the 02d1e01e code instead issued enable --now, which also did not reload). systemd-resolved only parses the new drop-in on start/reload. If nothing else already serves the just-installed address, Docker containers using it cannot resolve names until a separate reload/restart or reboot, yet the migrations and upgrade can report success. Base's pending historical migration issued restart, albeit swallowed failures. Reload/restart the resolver after changing its drop-ins on the upgrade path, separately from avoiding sudo for other users; do not depend on enable --now or on the later recovery migration (also skips an active service). On upgrades where the historical marker was already written, this lack of reload also existed before the PR.
leads.triage: dropped_after_opus_followup; Opus follow-up (opus/followup-resolved-reload.md): stock 3.8 already has identical Docker DNS drop-in with resolved restarted; only new content LLMNR=no; nothing pre-reboot breaks; difference from 1354a01a not 53149199.

leads.summary: The new regression test cannot detect removal of both historical migration call sites
leads.consequence: Replace both invocations of ensure_systemd_resolved in the historical migration with true while keeping the helper body as dead code: all its text assertions and recovery-only runtime checks still pass, but the historical migration once again retires networkd and marks complete without detecting a failed resolved start. Exercise the historical script under stubs with a stub resolv.conf, inactive/failing systemctl, and assert nonzero migration exit and absent completion marker. This is the previously noted test gap, still present at the new head.

limits: No live service, /etc or NetworkManager commands were run. Behavioural reproductions used only review.py sandbox stubs and modified source snapshots; upstream systemd files were read at v261.3, the version named in a related PR's DNS documentation, not verified as this machine's installed systemd version.

The repository-wide /usr ownership test fails equally on the pinned head and current base because the fetched latest PKGBUILD lacks the pre-existing /usr/share/owe/10-owe-sync install (plan5); neither failing line is in this PR. Broad GitHub topic searches return many unrelated open PRs; the overlapping runner, installer, upgrader and DNS PRs are recorded in inventory.json/open_prs.

flags.claim: resolved active, account without sudo rights: head exit 0, no `sudo` call
flags.why: Head N1 exited 0 with the marker, but the migration still made 10 sudo calls (NetworkManager enable --now, networkd disable/mask/stop, NetworkManager reload), all swallowed by `|| true`. Only resolved was left alone: the one resolved call was `systemctl is-active --quiet systemd-resolved.service`.
flags.disposition: fixed; row 1 'no sudo call' -> 'resolved not touched'

flags.claim: resolved active with `sudo` denied (expect exit 0 and no `sudo` call)
flags.why: Same as F1. Running the whole migration makes the swallowed sudo calls at lines 104-115, so a test that asserts no sudo call would fail. My own final report has the same error in its R2-T1 section (an inconsistency in my report, carried into the draft).
flags.disposition: fixed; test expectation -> no systemctl enable --now systemd-resolved.service call

flags.claim: Only then does it call `sudo systemctl enable --now` and require `is-active`.
flags.why: Ambiguous and slightly too strong. 'Only then' grammatically points back at the early-return conditions, which is the opposite of the meaning. The call also goes through `as_root`, which runs the command directly when EUID is 0 and through sudo otherwise (lines 3-9, 32).
flags.disposition: fixed; 'Only then does it call sudo ...' -> 'Otherwise it runs ... through as_root (so through sudo for a normal user)'

flags.claim: writes the stub link before migrations run, so a resolved that cannot start still fails that run (also the qualifier in table line 12)
flags.why: The outcome holds, but not always through this migration. `1782002156` calls ensure_systemd_resolved only on the non-live branch (line 116) and on the live branch when NetworkManager is already active (line 86). On the live branch with NetworkManager inactive (lines 87-97; the upgrade only enables NM at upgrade line 1389), it never calls it, so head exits 0 with no resolved calls, the same as base. The upgrade's migration pass still fails there, through the recovery migration `1790048120` in the same `omarchy-migrate` run: it does not check the live flag, the stub link is present, and a failed `enable --now` exits non-zero (lines 24-38). That last point comes from source plus the PR test's enable-fails case passing at head. I did not run the recovery migration through the runner in live mode in this round.
flags.disposition: fixed; failure attributed to this migration when NM running, otherwise recovery migration

flags.claim: the new check skips only a redundant `enable`, because the upgrade has already enabled the unit
flags.why: Minor. `enable_system_service` only warns if `systemctl enable` fails (upgrade line 1271). 'Has already enabled' assumes success. When the enable failed and resolved is running anyway, head leaves it disabled where 02d1e01e enabled it (N12). Low impact.
flags.disposition: fixed; 'already enabled the unit' -> 'already run systemctl enable on the unit'

flags.claim: isolated runs of the migrations through the real runner
flags.why: Minor. In this round only the historical migration (plus a dummy later migration) ran through `bin/omarchy-migrate`. The recovery migration was exercised only through the PR's test, which pipes it into `bash -euo pipefail`.
flags.disposition: fixed; test scope: historical migration through the real runner

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12909#issuecomment-5855882788) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12909#issuecomment-5857409671), checked at head `53149199`.

**Verified:** The historical-migration issue from the previous review is resolved. The test gap and the PR description note from that review still apply. No regression from `53149199` was found on the Quattro upgrade path.

| Earlier finding | Status at `53149199` |
|---|---|
| Recovery skips the upgrade's relative stub link | **Resolved** (recovery migration unchanged since `02d1e01e`) |
| Historical migration propagates a failed resolved start | **Still holds** when resolved is inactive and `/etc/resolv.conf` is the stub link |
| Historical migration fails for accounts that cannot start resolved, even where it is not needed | **Resolved** |
| Optional test improvement: historical migration checked only by text | **Still applies**, now also to the new early returns |
| PR description names `1790044019` | **Still applies** |

**Verified:** [`ensure_systemd_resolved`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/531491999f4741e3bbe26fd9f1fcdc7861a02e46/migrations/1782002156.sh#L14-L37) now returns early when resolved is already active, and when `/etc/resolv.conf` is not a symlink to either stub spelling. Otherwise it runs `systemctl enable --now` through `as_root` (so through `sudo` for a normal user) and requires `is-active`. This is the same stub check the recovery migration uses. Isolated runs of the non-live branch through the real migration runner, with stubbed `sudo` and `systemctl`:

| Host state | Head `53149199` | Previous `02d1e01e` | Base `7b336b1b` |
|---|---|---|---|
| resolved active, account without sudo rights | exit 0, resolved not touched | exit 1 | exit 0 |
| regular `resolv.conf` file, resolved masked | exit 0 | exit 1 | exit 0 |
| relative stub link, resolved fails to start | exit 1, marker not written | exit 1 | exit 0 |
| relative stub link, resolved inactive, account without sudo rights | exit 1 | exit 1 | exit 0 |

The last row fails because DNS depends on resolved in that state. During the Quattro upgrade, [`omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/531491999f4741e3bbe26fd9f1fcdc7861a02e46/bin/omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro#L1374) writes the stub link before migrations run, so a resolved that cannot start still fails the upgrade's migrations: in this migration when NetworkManager is already running, otherwise in the recovery migration. On the upgrade's live branch with NetworkManager active and resolved already running, the new check skips only a redundant `enable`, because the upgrade has already run `systemctl enable` on the unit.

**Pre-existing:** The reply's wording ("accounts without sudo no longer fail the historical migration") holds for `ensure_systemd_resolved`. Other steps of `1782002156.sh` still use `sudo` without a fallback: moving stock networkd files, and installing NetworkManager when it is missing. With resolved active, no sudo rights and a stock `20-ethernet.network` present, the migration exits 1 on head, previous head and base alike.

**Optional test improvement:** `test/shell.d/systemd-resolved-migration-test.sh` is unchanged and still checks `1782002156.sh` only by text. With the head's historical migration changed in any of these ways, it still passes:

- both `ensure_systemd_resolved` call sites replaced with `true`
- `return 0` as the function's first line
- the new early returns removed (the `02d1e01e` version)

Running `1782002156.sh` itself with the `systemctl` stub would cover both the fix and the failure path. For example: stub link with a failing start (expect non-zero exit), resolved active with `sudo` denied (expect exit 0 and no `systemctl enable --now systemd-resolved.service` call), and regular `resolv.conf` with resolved masked (expect exit 0). Such a run needs `/etc/resolv.conf` and `/etc/systemd/network` redirected into the test directory, a `NetworkManager` stub on PATH and a `sudo` stub that can refuse.

**Documentation:** The PR description still names the recovery migration `1790044019`; the file is `1790048120.sh`. Its first bullet ("`enable --now`s resolved and exits if the unit stays inactive") now applies only when resolved is inactive and `/etc/resolv.conf` is the stub link.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Head `53149199`, compared with the previous head `02d1e01e` and the merge-base `7b336b1b`. Source inspection, plus isolated runs of the historical migration through the real runner and of the PR's test against modified copies of the historical migration, with stubbed `sudo` and service commands. The `sudo` stub models a refusal only, not a password prompt. No live systemd, DNS, NetworkManager or full upgrade run. Which accounts reach the non-live branch, and the upgrade's ordering, come from reading the source. The Quattro upgrade's final package sync still runs before migrations, so these checks do not cover DNS failures before migrations are reached.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
